summary: 3 positions closed: META target_hit (+14.7%, T2 at $660 cleared on AI cloud buildout momentum and TSMC +36% demand confirmation); NVDA puts stopped_out (-8.8%, NVDA closed $210.96 on July 10 triggering $200 stop; reconstitution exhaustion thesis failed as AI semis re-rated on SKHY debut and TSMC revenue beat); TLT expired (-3.4%, hawkish FOMC minutes July 8 reversed NFP-driven bond rally; Iran re-escalation reinforced oil-inflation-rate-hike channel). 3 new ideas added: long XOM (Iran/Hormuz escalation + Permian production insulation + Freeport LNG export upside; differentiated from XLE ETF already in book), long MU (HBM4 cycle confirmed by SKHY debut +12.7% above $149 IPO and TSMC +36% structural demand; MU is US-listed HBM4 comps to SKHY), short JETS (WTI spike from $69 to $73-74 destroys airline fuel-cost thesis; sector-wide short via ETF complementary to active DAL long). Regime: STEP ASIDE; TSMC +36% is the structural bull signal for AI semis; Iran/Hormuz is the dominant tape headwind; BTC Gate 2 ($62,000) in critical proximity (24h low $62,489); triple-stack July 14 event (CPI + Warsh testimony + 5 major bank earnings) warrants reduced position sizing.

closed_today.note: META surged from $609 (July 9) to $669.21 by July 13, clearing both T1 ($625) and T2 ($660) in 10 trading days from the July 3 entry at $583.50. Catalyst: Zuckerberg Meta AI cloud initiative reports surfaced July 1 plus TSMC Q2 +36% revenue confirming structural AI demand. T3 ($710) remains the Q2 earnings blue-sky scenario (expected July 29); the 20% tranche can be held toward T3.

NVDA closed $210.96 on July 10, breaching the $200 daily-close stop. The reconstitution exhaustion thesis failed: TSMC Q2 revenue +36% ($39.6B) and SKHY 7x oversubscription reset the AI semis multiple, pulling NVDA from $196 to $210+ in 9 sessions. The July 11 $190 puts expired deeply OTM and worthless. Actual loss was approximately 100% of put premium (~5% of notional, capped at premium paid per the defined-risk structure).

NFP July 2 printed 57K (below the 90K recession floor) and TLT initially rallied, but hawkish FOMC minutes July 8 (9/18 Fed members favored a hike; Warsh withheld dot) reversed all bond gains. Iran re-escalation on July 10-13 reinforced the oil-inflation-rate-hike channel. TLT never breached the $84 stop, but held $84.38 at the July 11 expiry — a loss from the $87.36 entry. Position expired per the 2-week time limit.
